title: Napoleon wasn't short
hook: Napoleon was about average height. The myth came from a mix-up over inches.
peek: Napoleon was recorded as 5 feet 2 inches, but in French units. Converted to English measures that is about 5 feet 7 inches, ordinary or a little tall for a Frenchman of his time. Cartoons did the rest.
lede: Napoleon Bonaparte is remembered as tiny, but he probably was not. At his death he was measured at 5 pieds 2 pouces, the old French feet and inches. A French inch was longer than an English one, so in English units he stood about 5 feet 7 inches, around 1.69 metres. That was roughly average, or a little above, for a Frenchman of his era.

bullets.text: Before the metric system, France measured with the king's foot, about 32.5 centimetres. Read in English units, the same numbers make a man sound several centimetres shorter than he was.
British cartoonists, above all James Gillray, drew Napoleon as a small, furious figure in a huge hat. The image stuck in English-speaking countries and outlasted the wars.
His soldiers called him le petit caporal, the little corporal. It was an affectionate nickname about his closeness to the ranks, not a comment on his size.
Napoleon was often seen beside his Imperial Guard, whose soldiers had to meet height requirements. Standing next to them, almost anyone would look short, and the impression travelled.
